name: Tessera Corponation Ocular Depth Compiler
description: The Ocular Depth Compiler is a paired replacement of the eye's vitreous chamber and retinal architecture, replacing the organic lens-and-receptor system with a multi-spectral sensor array behind a synthetic corneal lens that is optically indistinguishable from natural tissue. Where conventional ocular augmentations focus on visual enhancement — magnification, night vision, overlays — the Depth Compiler's core function is spatial reconstruction: it continuously builds a precise three-dimensional model of the user's environment by processing stereoscopic depth data across visible, near-infrared, and structured-light frequencies simultaneously, feeding this model to a co-processor implanted at the temporal lobe interface.
specifications: {"depth_resolution":"Sub-millimeter accuracy at 0–12m, centimeter accuracy at 12–60m","spectral_range":"380nm–1400nm continuous","environmental_model_refresh":"120Hz spatial update rate","co-processor_location":"Temporal lobe, surface-mount inductive interface","battery_life":"72 hours continuous on internal cell; passive solar supplementation via corneal photovoltaic layer","visual_acuity":"Equivalent to 20/8 natural vision in standard light","compatibility":"Tessera neural overlay stack recommended for full spatial model access"}
cultural_context: Tessera markets the Depth Compiler as an architectural and engineering tool, and a significant portion of its legal user base genuinely uses it that way — surveyors, construction planners, and disaster response teams in Meridian 88's constantly-shifting infrastructure zones. This legitimate use base gives the augmentation a veneer of professional respectability that other high-tier ocular mods lack. In social settings, users are often identified by a subtle tell: they tend to pause at the threshold of new rooms, a habit formed from the moment the spatial model initializes. Other augmented individuals sometimes read this as a dominance behavior — a predator cataloguing its environment.
known_users: Tessera Corponation field surveyors and infrastructure planners
Architectural saboteurs who plan structural collapses
story_hooks: A Depth Compiler user has inadvertently captured spatial data of a classified facility interior during what they thought was a routine survey job — now multiple parties want that data, and they don't understand why.

Tessera's co-processor firmware has a vulnerability that allows remote access to a user's live spatial model feed — someone has been watching through the eyes of the city's infrastructure workers for months.

A blind child in a low-tier district has been given a bootleg Depth Compiler by a well-meaning contact — but without the proper temporal lobe co-processor, the spatial data is causing severe neurological disruption.

The processing lag in complex environments has been exploited by a crew who designs ambush sites specifically calibrated to overload the Depth Compiler's model refresh, leaving the user effectively blind for 1.2 seconds.
